# `components/MaterialNodePresets.js`

> **Source:** `editor/js/components/MaterialNodePresets.js`

MaterialNodePresets.js - Pre-built node graph recipes for all built-in materials Each preset is a valid node graph using only standard MaterialNodeTypes nodes. These serve as demos showing users how to wire nodes to create materials. Graph structure: { nodes: [...], connections: [...], view: { panX, panY, zoom } } Node: { id, type, x, y, params } Connection: { fromNode, fromPort, toNode, toPort }

## Functions

### `getPresetGraph(materialId)`

Get the preset node graph for a built-in material.

**Parameters:**

- `materialId` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

**Returns:** Graph data { nodes, connections, view } or null

### `hasPresetGraph(materialId)`

Check if a material has a preset graph.

**Parameters:**

- `materialId` *(string)* — _No description in source JSDoc._

### `listPresetIds()`

List all material IDs that have preset graphs.

### `listSubstancePresetIds()`

Get all substance-linked preset IDs.

### `listAnimatedPresetIds()`

Get all animated effect preset IDs (lava, water, hologram, etc.).

## Constants

- `NODE_GRAPH_PRESETS`

## Notes & Examples

### Editor Extension System

The editor supports extensions via the same Plauna component system as apps. Extensions can add panels, tools, menu items, and hooks into the engine. They run with elevated 'editor' capability granting access to the scene graph, asset database, and build pipeline.

**Example: Editor extension adding a custom panel**
```js
import { Extension } from 'editor/core/Extension.js';
import { Panel } from 'editor/ui/Panel.js';

class TerrainEditor extends Extension {
  id = 'terrain-editor';
  capabilities = ['editor', 'scene'];
  
  activate(context) {
    // Add menu item
    context.menus.add('Tools/Terrain', () => this.open());
    
    // Register tool
    context.tools.register('terrain', {
      icon: 'mountain',
      onSelect: (entity) => this.edit(entity)
    });
  }
  
  open() {
    this.panel = new Panel({
      title: 'Terrain Editor',
      content: this.buildUI()
    });
    context.workspace.addPanel(this.panel);
  }
  
  edit(entity) {
    const terrain = entity.get(TerrainComponent);
    this.panel.bind(terrain);
  }
}

editor.extensions.register(TerrainEditor);
```
